t: Dynamic Website Builder - public implementations survey
title: Dynamic Website Builder - public implementations survey
definition: Creates websites whose content or behavior changes at runtime.
description:
Dynamic Website Builder is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Creates websites whose content or behavior changes at runtime. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Dynamic Website Builder. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Dynamic Website Builder. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Dynamic Website Builder capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: Lighthouse - related Dynamic Website Builder technology
title: Lighthouse - related Dynamic Website Builder technology
definition: Automated audits for performance and SEO.
description:
Lighthouse is not itself a Dynamic Website Builder, but it belongs in this survey because real Dynamic Website Builder work leans on it. Automated audits for performance and SEO.

In a Dynamic Website Builder build it shows up when startup speed beats raw peak power. The design favors boring reliability over cleverness: well-trodden paths, clear errors, and behavior you can reason about without reading the source. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best Dynamic Website Builder practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, Lighthouse is a strong default choice as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Dynamic Website B
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Dynamic Website B
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Dynamic Website Builder from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Dynamic Website Builder from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Dynamic Website Builder needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
